items.title: A pool that never allocates
items.question: Make the pool work without touching the heap after the constructor. The last test counts calls to `new`.

tests.setup: Pool p(3); int a = p.allocate(); int b = p.allocate(); p.allocate(); p.release(b);
Pool p(3); int a = p.allocate(); int b = p.allocate(); p.release(a); p.release(b);
Pool p(3); int a = p.allocate(); int b = p.allocate(); p.release(a); p.release(b); p.allocate();
Pool p(2); p.allocate(); p.allocate(); p.release(0); p.allocate();
Pool p(2); p.allocate(); p.allocate(); p.release(0); p.release(1);
Pool p(8); reset_alloc_count(); for (int r = 0; r < 100; ++r) { int s = p.allocate(); p.release(s); }

widget.how: Check runs 10 hidden tests. The last one counts the calls to `new` made while the pool runs, and expects none.

feedback.correct: The tests pass and the counter reads what it should.
feedback.generic: Some tests failed. Open the first one that failed below the editor.

items.title: A buffer that frees itself
items.question: Add what the buffer is missing so nothing leaks, and make `total()` stop allocating.

tests.setup: Buffer b(50); reset_alloc_count(); for (int r = 0; r < 20; ++r) b.total();

widget.how: Check runs 5 hidden tests. Two harness checks run beside them: every `new[]` must be matched by `delete[]`, and `total()` must not call `new`.
